title: Block-compact attention indexing and paged-KV merge heuristics
content:
Context:
We keep seeing tail latency spikes when long-sequence chat workloads trigger repeated paged-KV fetches. Current paged-KV design treats pages as independent fixed-size slabs; the runtime issues a full page load on misses and evicts whole pages on pressure. FlashAttention kernels expect compact, contiguous KV chunks for high throughput. The mismatch causes 3 sources of inefficiency:

1) Sparse token distributions cause many small KV ranges to be loaded across pages (fragmentation).
2) Kernel-level prolog/epilog overhead increases when KV is split across pages (multiple kernel launches to stitch KV).
3) Eviction-induced churn: hot-but-sparse keys bounce between memory tiers causing repeated page flips.

Problem statement:
Design a lightweight compaction/indexing layer that:
- Compacts scattered per-request KV references into contiguous blocks for the attention kernel (no model change).
- Minimizes extra copy overhead (prefer in-place or single memcpy per request if possible).
- Works with paged-KV: supports trivial merge/overlay of partial pages into compact buffers for FlashAttention-style kernels.
- Cooperates with existing eviction heuristics to avoid creating long-lived heavy compaction artifacts.

Goals and constraints:
- Keep extra per-request latency < 0.5ms 95th for 8k context on A100-class instance (goal).
- Avoid global stop-the-world operations; must be asynchronous-safe.
- Memory overhead should be bounded: transient compaction buffer pool with capacity budgeted per-GPU.
- Backwards compatible with current kernel API shapes (q,k,v pointers + lengths).

High-level approach:
1) Index-collect phase (host or device): build a small metadata vector of (page_id, offset, length, dest_offset). This is tiny compared to token data.
2) Page-merge planner: on collection, compute contiguous segments by coalescing adjacent ranges that fall into the same physical page or adjacent pages. Use simple heuristics: merge if gap < G tokens (G tunable), or if merging reduces number of DMA ops by >= 2.
3) Compaction copy: issue an asynchronous device memcpy (or GPU kernel memcpy) for each merged segment into a preallocated per-stream compaction slab. Because most merges reduce the number of DMA ops, the net effect reduces tail.
4) Kernel invocation: run FlashAttention variant that consumes the compact slab as a single contiguous KV buffer; kernel still gets per-head offsets via short per-request metadata.
5) Release slab to pool when ready; track slab GC via cuda events to avoid premature reuse.

Pseudocode (host-side planner):

// collected_refs: list of (page_id, start_token, end_token)
function plan_compaction(collected_refs):
  sort collected_refs by (page_id, start_token)
  result = []
  current = null
  for r in collected_refs:
    if current == null:
      current = copy(r)
      continue
    gap = r.start_token - current.end_token
    if r.page_id == current.page_id or gap <= G:
      // merge
      current.end_token = r.end_token
      continue
    else:
      result.append(compact_segment_from(current))
      current = copy(r)
  if current != null:
    result.append(compact_segment_from(current))
  return result

Kernel sketch (device-side tiny helper to remap offsets):
- input: compacted_kv_buf, meta[] = {(head_offset, token_count, per_head_stride)}
- FlashAttention loads KV by head; meta drives ldG memory reads
- Important: maintain original global token ids to compute positional bias/ALiBi if used

Micro-optimizations and tricks:
- Fuse compaction with quantized dequant path: if pages are quantized int8 and kernel wants fp16, perform dequant + copy in a single kernel to avoid round-trips.
- For tiny ranges (< 16 tokens) prefer coalesced GPU kernel that packs multiple tiny ranges into one warp to amortize overhead.
- Use persistent thread blocks for compactor kernel to keep warm state (allocator index) and avoid malloc overhead.
- When page data is already contiguous in device memory (rare), skip copy and supply gathered offsets to FlashAttention. Kernel path supports both contiguous buffer and scatter-gather offsets.

Interaction with eviction and cache policy:
- Compaction slabs are transient and should not extend page residency; i.e., compaction MUST be read-only with no page pinning beyond necessary. We should not treat compacted slabs as a new long-lived cache.
- Eviction hints: increase recency/touch score for pages that are frequently merged; these pages likely contain hot keys. Use a moving-average score with decay constant tau.
- Avoid promoting pages simply because they were part of a huge compaction once. Implement a promotion threshold (e.g., touched > N times in T seconds).

Scheduling and batching implications:
- Compaction planner should operate per-batch; for multi-request batching, coalesce across requests when they reference overlapping pages to create larger contiguous copies. This helps throughput but increases tail for individual queries — provide a SLA knob.
- Priority-aware compaction: if a request is latency-critical (priority flag), do minimal merging (fast path) and let the kernel run on slightly fragmented KV; for throughput/cheap requests, run aggressive compaction to maximize kernel efficiency.

Memory accounting and fallback paths:
- Preallocate slab pool: e.g., 4 slabs of size S per GPU. Slab sizes are power-of-two multiples of 256KB tuned from profiling.
- Fallback: if slab pool exhausted, fallback to scatter-gather kernel that accepts an array of pointers (lower throughput but avoids blocking). Avoid stalling request queues.

Profiling plan / metrics to collect:
- Per-request: number of refs, pre-merge DMA ops, post-merge DMA ops, compaction copy time, kernel execution time, total latency.
- Per-page stats: merge_count, touch_count, avg_merge_size, eviction_count.
- Global: slab pool utilization, slab contention wait times, 95th/99th latency delta vs baseline.

Benchmarks to run (minimal initial set):
1) Synthetic dense: contiguous KV, measure baseline FlashAttention vs compacted (should be equal or slightly worse due to copy).
2) Sparse hotspots: many small ranges across pages; expect compaction to reduce number of DMAs and latency tail.
3) Chat-like churn: repeated near-hot keys causing eviction; measure churn reduction and access pattern changes.

Open implementation questions / TODOs:
- Q: Where does planning run best? Host thread (low CPU cost but PCIe round-trip) vs device microkernel (requires specialized kernels but can eliminate host-to-device roundtrip). Need microbenchmarks.
- Q: How to represent merged metadata compactly so the FlashAttention kernel overhead is minimal? Suggest a packed 64-bit descriptor per segment.
- Q: Integration with quantization: ensure single-step dequant+compact kernel for int8-backed pages. Prototype needed.
- TODO: Prototype planner in C++ host + CUDA memcpy path. Measure P95 for 8k chat workload. (Owner: Ava)
- TODO: Build scatter-gather FlashAttn fallback kernel and add runtime switch. (Owner: Ravi)
- TODO: Add perf counters (GPU timestamps) and slab pool tracing. (Owner: Marisol)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight Bloom filter per-page to speed skip checks when planning merges across many pages. Might help for extreme-scale page tables.
- If compaction planning becomes heavy, push it to a dedicated lightweight planner thread pool to avoid stalling inference worker threads.
- Could combine with rerouting policy: if compaction cost > estimated kernel win, route the request to a higher-cost dedicated GPU pool (Dedicated) where bigger slabs are available.

References and related work:
- FlashAttention design notes (internal)
- Prior paged-KV eviction RFC (see JIRA-RT-512)
- External: "Efficient Sparse Attention on GPUs" (paper notes in drive link)

Appendix: quick microbench sketch for merge heuristic tuning:
- Sweep G in {0,4,8,16,32}
- For each G, run 10k requests sampled from production traces and collect: mean DMA ops/request, mean merged_size, P95 latency. Pick G that minimizes P95 plus small penalty for extra copy bytes.

End-of-file.

(Unresolved: name for the compacted slab allocator API — suggestions: kv_compact_pool_t, slab_compactor, or kv_merge_ring.)
